title: The billing PR added a PATCH /api/subscription endpoint that takes the target customer's email from a query parameter instead of the logged-in user, so any authenticated user can cancel or resume anyone's Stripe subscription.

findings.explanation: All database access uses Django ORM query methods (filter, create, asave) with parameters supplied as function arguments. The ORM automatically parameterises queries, so no raw SQL concatenation is present.

Functions `get_user_subscription` and `set_user_subscription` accept an arbitrary email address and return or modify the subscription record for that email without any ownership or permission check. If these functions are exposed through an API endpoint, a malicious user could supply another user's email and retrieve or alter their subscription (IDOR). The diff does not show the surrounding endpoint code, so the flaw is plausible but not confirmed.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce that the caller can only access their own subscription (e.g., use request.user.email instead of a supplied email) or require proper admin permissions. Add explicit authorization checks before returning or modifying a Subscription record.
